summary:
The article surveys major events in the art world in 2021, a year marked by record sales, new public artworks, major exhibitions, and the return of in-person art fairs.

Sandro Botticelli’s *Portrait of a Young Man Holding a Roundel* sold for $92.2 million in January. Beeple’s NFT *Everydays: The First 5000 Days* brought $69.35 million at Christie’s in March. Frida Kahlo’s *Diego and I* sold for $34.9 million in November, setting a record for a Latin American artist. Frieze New York opened in May, the city’s first major art fair in more than a year.

Other notable events included the recovery of paintings stolen from Greece’s National Gallery, the opening of the Church arts center in Sag Harbor, and Banksy’s *A Great British Spraycation* works in eastern England. Museums and galleries presented exhibitions of artists including Alice Neel, Yayoi Kusama, Jasper Johns, and Andy Warhol. The article also records public art, films, an award, and the deaths of artists, curators, critics, and collectors.
